papers.title: Quality of life in andrology: a scoping review of original human studies.
papers.journal: Archivio italiano di urologia, andrologia : organo ufficiale [di] Societa italiana di ecografia urologica e nefrologica
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Andrological and male urologic conditions can reshape daily life in ways that are not captured by laboratory, anatomical or technical endpoints. Fertility plans, sexual confidence, body image, continence, intimate relationships and the burden of treatment may all matter as much as symptom relief. OBJECTIVE: To map original human studies reporting quality of life (QoL) or closely related patient-reported outcomes across eight clinical topics: male infertility, erectile dysfunction, ejaculatory dysfunction, Peyronie disease, hypogonadism, varicocele, penile cancer and ejaculation-sparing surgery for benign prostatic obstruction (BPO). METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 11 September 2026 for the original six andrology topics. A targeted PubMed and backward-citation update through 18 October 2026 added penile cancer and ejaculation- sparing BPO surgery. Eligible reports were randomized studies, observational cohorts, registries, cross-sectional or casecontrol studies, qualitative studies and instrument-development work in adult men. For penile cancer, QoL had to be analyzed directly, including explicit QoL-focused multidomain assessments or life satisfaction; sexual, urinary, aesthetic or reconstructive outcomes alone were deemed insufficient. In the BPO domain, surgery had to be explicitly ejaculation-sparing and QoL had to be measured directly. Reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, editorials, case reports and non-human studies were excluded from the evidence map. Two reviewers independently screened and charted eligible reports. RESULTS: Sixty-five original reports were included: seven instrument- development or validation studies and 58 condition-focused reports. papers.title: Family Ties and Well-Being in Older Adults: The Role of Rehabilitation Outcomes in Medicare Beneficiaries From a Longitudinal NHATS Study.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Family ties are important social determinants of rehabilitation and well-being in later life; however, their role as contextual factors in rehabilitation has not been sufficiently explored. This study examined whether different types of family ties are associated with well-being among older adults and whether rehabilitation outcomes mediate these associations. METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal analysis using data from the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) Rounds 12-14. The analytic sample included 4411 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 65 years. Family ties were categorized into four groups (kinless, disconnected, distanced, and close) in Round 12, with kinless as the reference group. Rehabilitation outcomes were assessed in Round 13 and were available only for participants who reported receiving rehabilitation services. Well-being was assessed in Round 14 using a composite measure of affective well-being, meaning and purpose, and sense of control. Structural equation modeling accounting for complex survey design was used to estimate direct and indirect associations. RESULTS: Compared with the kinless group, close family ties were consistently associated with higher well-being, whereas disconnected and distanced ties did not differ significantly. All three rehabilitation outcomes were significantly associated with well-being. However, a significant indirect effect was observed only for goal attainment after rehabilitation and only in the close family ties group. The direct association between close family ties and well-being remained significant after accounting for the mediator. CONCLUSIONS: Family ties, particularly close relationships, were associated with well-being among older adults, and goal attainment after rehabilitation partially mediated this association. papers.title: The fertility crisis and post-labor social architecture: Why Elon Musk should build FamilyLand.
papers.journal: Politics and the life sciences : the journal of the Association for Politics and the Life Sciences
papers.abstract: Low fertility partly reflects a weakening of the pathway through which attraction leads to pair-bonding and childbearing. Modern mating ecologies allow mating to remain active while making family-forming partnerships harder to achieve, producing a Post-Pair-Bonding Fertility Trap. This article uses that evolutionary diagnosis to develop FamilyLand, an institutional prototype for post-labor life, in which residents would be freed from economically necessary work. Private family life would be embedded within communities designed to strengthen social connections, make childrearing less isolating, and make family formation more attractive and fulfilling. FamilyLand would simulate a future of AI-enabled material abundance before it exists society-wide, testing whether such conditions can strengthen pair-bonding and fertility realization rather than deepen social isolation. Elon Musk is identified as the clearest candidate to build FamilyLand because he combines the technological resources and capacity to realize such an ambitious project with a deep concern about declining fertility.

papers.title: From Thought to Threat: Examining CSA Fantasy Expression in Incel Online Discourse.
papers.abstract: Involuntary celibates (incels) are members of an online subculture consisting primarily of men who hold resentment and misogynistic beliefs as a result of their perceived inability to form sexual or romantic relationships with women. Recent research has identified a concerning shift in incel discourse: beyond sexual entitlement toward adult women, some users have been found to sexualize underage girls. Accordingly, the present study examines how child sexual abuse (CSA) fantasies are expressed and justified within this context. The present study conducted a content analysis and a thematic analysis of user-provided justifications for their CSA fantasies on an incel forum. Results showed that fantasy content most frequently centered on pubescent girls and combined themes of domination and romantic connection. Justifications clustered around compensatory desire, misogynistic rejection, appeals to purity or tradition, biological inevitability, and exploratory curiosity. Overall, the findings suggest that CSA fantasies in this setting are embedded within broader ideological narratives circulating in incel communities, including grievance, sexual entitlement, and perceived male dispossession. Implications and further directions are discussed.

papers.title: Structural Regulation of Ether/Amino Acid Ionic Liquid Biphasic Solvents for Highly Efficient CO2 Capture.
papers.abstract: Biphasic CO2 absorbents reduce regeneration energy by regenerating only the CO2-rich phase, but high viscosity and poorly controlled phase separation still limit their performance. To address these challenges, diethylenetriamine (DETA) was employed as the primary reactive absorbent, and the effects of the structures of glycol ethers and amino acid ionic liquids on the CO2 absorption performance of DEDM-DETA-water-AAIL (DDWA) biphasic solvents were systematically investigated. The results demonstrated that, compared with long-chain ethers, branched ethers, and hydroxyl-containing glycol ethers, the short-chain linear glycol ether (DEDM) more effectively promoted the enrichment of CO2 reaction products in the CO2-rich phase. Among the amino acid anions investigated, the serinate anion ([Ser]-), containing a short hydroxyl-functionalized side chain, outperformed glycinate and lysinate ([Lys]-) anions by enhancing CO2 absorption through the synergistic effects of amino reactive sites and hydrogen-bonding interactions while simultaneously reducing the viscosity of the CO2-rich phase. The optimized DDWA absorbent exhibited a CO2 dynamic uptake of 2.72 mol kg-1, representing a 12% increase over the ionic liquid-free system. In addition, the absorbent showed excellent cyclic stability, with a total regeneration energy consumption of only 1.78 GJ t-1 CO2. Spectroscopic analyses revealed that the absorption products derived from DETA and [Ser] were predominantly enriched in the lower phase, whereas DEDM remained the principal component of the upper phase. This strategy couples alcohol-ether induced phase separation with AAIL regulation, enabling synergistic optimization of absorption, phase separation, and regeneration.

papers.title: Phase-field modeling of multi-flake growth and grain-boundary formation in CVD-grown 2D materials.
papers.abstract: Controlling domain morphology and grain-boundary formation is essential for tailoring the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD). Here, we develop a three-field phase-field framework for the concurrent growth and impingement of multiple 2D flakes. The model couples a phase field delineating the flake, a surface adatom concentration field, and a continuous orientation field describing the crystallographic orientation of individual domains. By varying the effective adatom supply flux, surface diffusivity, and characteristic attachment timescale, we identify how competition between adatom transport and boundary attachment governs flake morphology. Lower diffusivity and faster attachment favor narrow, three-armed, star-like structures, whereas enhanced adatom redistribution or slower attachment promotes compact triangular domains. Increasing the adatom supply flux reduces the relative nonuniformity of the concentration field and produces rounded, compact morphologies. In multi-flake systems, overlapping adatom-depletion zones generate growth competition and modify the evolution of neighboring domains, while the orientation field resolves impingement and grain-boundary formation between misoriented flakes. Using the collision configurations of Artyukhov et al. as a benchmark, the model reproduces their bowtie-like bicrystals. Collision maps that vary the position and nucleation delay of a second flake show when an arrow-shaped rather than a bowtie bicrystal forms, and that a flake nucleating next to an edge of an earlier one, inside its adatom-depletion zone, reaches only about 40% of the area of the earlier flake, compared with 90% for independent growth. This computationally efficient continuum framework provides a qualitative mesoscale description relating kinetic growth parameters to domain morphology and polycrystalline microstructure.

papers.title: Subsurface stabilization of sulfur species from SO2 uptake on ice surfaces.
papers.abstract: Ice surfaces play an important role in atmospheric sulfur cycling, yet the mechanisms governing SO2 uptake and transformation remain poorly understood. Here, we combine depth-resolved ambient pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) with O K-edge near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) spectroscopy to probe sulfur speciation and the interfacial environment at the vapor-ice interface. By varying the probing depth, we show that SO2-derived sulfur is confined to the upper few nanometers but exhibits a non-monotonic depth profile. Sulfur is observed predominantly as a single species, with S 2p binding energies consistent with a bisulfite-like S(IV) species, most plausibly HSO3-. The non-monotonic depth dependence is consistent with preferential sulfur enrichment below the outermost surface-sensitive region. NEXAFS measurements reveal that SO2 exposure perturbs the hydrogen-bonding network, increasing interfacial disorder without producing a uniform quasi-liquid layer. Time-resolved measurements show that sulfur remains detectable after SO2 exposure ends, indicating non-instantaneous removal from the near-surface region. These results show that SO2 uptake involves coupled interfacial reaction, surface exchange, and short-range transport, leading to stabilization of sulfur-containing species within near-surface ice domains. More broadly, the findings reveal ice interfaces as vertically stratified, chemically heterogeneous reactive media that cannot be described solely by surface adsorption or bulk solubility. Sulfur dioxide gas undergoes uptake and transformation at the dynamic ice surface, then diffuses and becomes enriched below the surface, leading to subsurface sulfur stabilization where ice interfaces function as stratified reactive media.

papers.title: Strategies for adoption of smart hospitals: a systematic review and meta-synthesis.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT: To synthesise qualitative evidence on the strategies, facilitators and barriers influencing the adoption of smart hospitals—healthcare institutions that integrate artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things and electronic health records to optimise clinical processes—and to develop a comprehensive conceptual model of smart hospital implementation. DESIGN: Systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis, conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 and the Enhancing Transparency in Reporting the Synthesis of Qualitative Research (ENTREQ) guidelines, and pre-registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261410449). DATA SOURCES: Eight electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, ProQuest, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore and the Cochrane Library) were searched from inception to March 2026, supplemented by reference-list hand-searching and grey-literature searches. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Peer-reviewed qualitative and mixed-methods studies published in English from inception to March 2026 that involved stakeholders engaged in smart hospital adoption and reported findings on implementation, adoption, strategies, facilitators, barriers, experiences or organisational impacts. Studies were selected using the Sample, Phenomenon of Interest, Design, Evaluation, Research type (SPIDER) framework. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Two reviewers independently screened, extracted and appraised studies; methodological quality was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme Qualitative Studies Checklist. Data were synthesised using Thomas and Harden’s three-stage thematic synthesis, and confidence in the synthesised findings was evaluated using the Confidence in the Evidence from Reviews of Qualitative Research (CERQual) framework. papers.title: Ascending somatosensory systems processing affiliative social touch.
papers.abstract: Affiliative social touch is a fundamental channel of mammalian communication that influences attachment, parenting, social buffering, play, and reproduction. Traditionally, somatosensory research focused on discriminative properties of touch, while later studies emphasized affective touch mediated by C-tactile afferents and related pathways. Here, we propose a broader framework in which affiliative social touch is understood not as a specialized affective modality but as a multidimensional social signal whose meaning depends on context, internal state, social relationship, and behavioral goals. Drawing primarily on rodent models, we review the ascending somatosensory systems that convey affiliative tactile information from the periphery to the brain. We discuss the contributions of low-threshold mechanoreceptors, the vibrissal system, and also spinal circuits that begin transforming tactile signals into affectively relevant representations. We further examine parallel ascending pathways through the brainstem, thalamus, and cortex, highlighting the roles of the parabrachial nucleus, posterior intralaminar thalamic nucleus, hypothalamic and limbic networks, and cortical systems involved in sensory processing, salience detection, and social cognition. Neuromodulatory systems, including oxytocin, endogenous opioids, dopamine, and serotonin, which shape the behavioral interpretation of affiliative social touch are also discussed. Finally, we consider the conservation of these mechanisms in human. The paper argues that affiliative social touch is not encoded by dedicated pathways for specific social behaviors; rather, common somatosensory signals gain social meaning through interactions with distributed neural circuits and state-dependent modulatory mechanisms. Understanding how ascending somatosensory pathways transform affiliative social contact into socially meaningful representations provides a unifying framework for investigating the neural basis of social behavior.

papers.title: Sex-stratified associations of parenthood, child number, and youngest-child age with sexual function and psychosocial well-being.
papers.abstract: Parenthood reorganizes time, sleep, psychological load, and couple intimacy, but its sexual correlates may differ by sex and stage of child development. In this cross-sectional mixed clinic/community convenience sample, 487 married adults were included: 208 women (153 mothers, 55 childless) and 279 men (221 fathers, 58 childless). Female sexual function was assessed with a modified six-item Female Sexual Function Index score; male outcomes included the five-item International Index of Erectile Function and the Premature Ejaculation Diagnostic Tool. After multivariable adjustment, motherhood was associated with a lower modified Female Sexual Function Index score (adjusted mean difference -6.19, 95% confidence interval -8.69 to -3.69), higher Insomnia Severity Index score (8.55, 7.07 to 10.03), and lower weekly sexual frequency (-1.62, -1.99 to -1.26). Fatherhood was associated with a higher Premature Ejaculation Diagnostic Tool score (4.32, 3.16 to 5.48) and lower sexual frequency (-1.77, -2.03 to -1.51), but not with erectile-function score after adjustment. Parenthood was associated with sex-specific sexual profiles, while youngest-child age appeared more informative than child number for maternal sexual function and sleep.

papers.title: "All Hope Is Not Lost:" The interplay between internalized gay ageism, body image, and sexual satisfaction.
papers.abstract: Sexual well-being is generally still understood as the absence of disease, despite established associations between physical health, mental health, sexual well-being, and sexual satisfaction. Little research has explored sexual satisfaction among older gay men, and a more in-depth understanding of sexual satisfaction is needed among this aging population, to improve their overall health. Thus, the purpose of this study was to explore experiences of internalized gay ageism among older gay men and how any such experiences and body image may influence sexual satisfaction. Qualitative interviews were conducted with 12 older gay men via Zoom or in-person, and these interviews were transcribed, recorded, and thematically analyzed. Three themes were generated throughout the thematic analysis, relating to internalized gay ageism, body image, and sexual satisfaction. The first identified theme was (a) "everybody's different" and so are experiences with ageism and homophobia, with three subthemes: ageism in the gay community leads to becoming "less desirable as I age," internalized homophobia is gendered and stifling "it's okay to be gay, just don't act it," and older gay men experience "invisibility" due to internalized intersectional prejudice. Additional main themes included (b) self-appraisal and partners shape body image, "respect for myself" and sexual satisfaction, and (c) understanding of sexual satisfaction and "the connection element" is varied and multifaceted, with a subtheme: sexual satisfaction shifts with age, as emotional connection becomes "more important." Implications are provided for future practice and research with older gay men, to promote health and well-being.
